newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Hoechst mulls shares-for-wages plan.
newsitem.headline: German Hoechst mulls shares-for-wages plan.

text.p: German chemicals group Hoechst AG said on Wednesday it was considering a profit-sharing scheme under which its employees would receive shares in the company in return for moderation in future wage demands.

A Hoechst spokesman confirmed in response to enquiries that its chief executive Juergen Dormann had mentioned the broad outline of such a plan in an interview with the weekly "Die Zeit" due to be published on Thursday.
"But no details have been worked out yet," he said, adding that the scheme was still only being considered as a possibility.
Other German companies such as the airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG have also said they are interested in applying such schemes to make their workforce more profit-oriented and to reduce wage costs.

But Hoechst, whose shares have doubled in value since spring 1995, said it did not intend that any such scheme should replace collectively-negotiated wage deals in the chemical sector, where the next round of 1997 wage talks start Thursday.
"We must naturally take into account the whole wage negotiation situation," the spokesman said.
